content.text: This is the classic OWASP Benchmark path traversal test case: `param` comes from a cookie value (user-controlled), decoded, concatenated into a file path and used to open a `FileInputStream` with no path validation/canonicalization/sanitization. This is a genuine path injection vulnerability.

input.justification: The value `param` is derived from a cookie supplied by the HTTP request (`request.getCookies()` -> `theCookie.getValue()`), URL-decoded, and concatenated directly onto a base directory to form `fileName`, which is then passed to `new java.io.File(fileName)` / `FileInputStream`. There is no validation, canonicalization, or allow-listing of the cookie value before it is used to construct the file path, so an attacker can supply path traversal sequences (e.g., ../../) in the cookie value to read arbitrary files accessible to the application. This matches the standard OWASP Benchmark path-traversal vulnerable test pattern.
